name: The Names
label: Factory Records
lede: A band of Brussels students handed Joy Division's manager a single at a gig, shook hands with Tony Wilson on a deal, and made their records with Martin Hannett, a toy xylophone included.

eras.title: The Passengers win a punk contest
eras.text: Marc Deprez and Michel Sordinia started the band in Brussels at Christmas 1977, as university students playing [[The Velvet Underground|Velvet Underground]] and Richard Hell covers. Two members left, Sordinia took the mic as well as the bass, and the songs got stranger.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Deprez and Sordinia form the Passengers in Brussels
years.p: With a second guitarist, Robert Franckson, and singer Isabelle Hanrez, the line-up drew Blondie comparisons. Christophe Den Tandt joined on drums.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: The Passengers win the First Belgian Punk Contest and refuse the prize
years.p: The prize was a single deal. They turned it down.

years.cap: The Passengers at Salle Aurore, Brussels, April 21, 1979
years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Supporting Magazine at the Ancienne Belgique
years.p: Opening for [[Magazine|043324ca-100d-48ce-8c7c-fd015afc103b]] in Brussels gave them their first proper soundcheck and the use of the Manchester band's light show.

years.cap: The Names at the Ancienne Belgique, Brussels, December 23, 1979
years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: The Passengers become the Names, and WEA puts out their demo
years.p: Spotting another Passengers in the NME, they became the Names. WEA's Belgian office released their own demo of "Spectators of Life" rather than re-record it with a producer.
years.xp: The single was backed with "White Life" and "The Drive". LTM calls it too commercial for post-punk fans and too odd for the mainstream; it became a collector's item.

eras.title: A handshake with Factory
eras.text: Joy Division's visit to Brussels put the Names in front of Rob Gretton, and by summer they were in Stockport with Martin Hannett. The Brussels end of Factory was growing at the same time, with Factory Benelux and Les Disques du Crépuscule.

years.cap: The Names at Place des Sciences, Louvain-la-Neuve, April 21, 1980
years.src: LTM: The Names · El Garaje de Frank
years.h: Sordinia hands Rob Gretton a single at Joy Division's Plan K show
years.p: [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] played Plan K in Brussels, and Sordinia gave their manager a copy of "Spectators of Life". Fiction was interested too, but Gretton came back with a Factory single deal.
years.xp:
[[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]] sealed it in April, in Brussels for [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]] and [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]] at Plan K. "Yes, a handshake with Tony Wilson!" the band told El Garaje de Frank. "They did that sort of things, at Factory's."

Gretton also passed on a message: "Martin loves you guys!"

years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: The Names miss a Manchester gig, and New Order debut in their place
years.p: Bad communications meant the Names never made their slot opening for A Certain Ratio at the Beach Club. [[Stephen Morris|b3036249-8b39-4d02-a312-d31a63497bbc]], [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]] and [[Bernard Sumner|6fa2e161-200e-475a-8492-3755594581f9]] played instead: [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]]'s first show after Joy Division.

years.src: LTM: The Names · El Garaje de Frank
years.h: Hannett hands Den Tandt a toy xylophone
years.p: With new drummer Luc Capelle, the Names met Hannett at Strawberry Studios in Stockport and cut both sides of their Factory single in one night. Den Tandt played the toy xylophone on "Nightshift" and Deprez shook his guitar as he played.
years.xp: Capelle had taken over the drums when Den Tandt moved to keyboards. Money was tight and Hannett worked his own way, so the band weren't there for the final mix. They liked what he did with it anyway, LTM says: a "majestic sound".

years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: "Nightshift" is FAC 29
years.p: A 7-inch only, with "I Wish I Could Speak Your Language" on the back. By summer 1981 it had sold more than 4,500 copies and reached No. 35 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp:
Ian Wright's sleeve drew on the B-side: people at a party, talking. When the distributor Pinnacle complained that Factory couldn't make it a hit, Wilson answered that Factory was "not a record company, but that's another story..."

Like [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]] and [[Crispy Ambulance|3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3]], the Names took reviews calling them Joy Division copyists. Two videos were made for the song; one, shot in their Brussels rehearsal room, is on A Factory Video.

years.cap: The Names at the Auditoire Paul-Emile Janson, Brussels University, October 31, 1980
years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Factory night at Brussels University; "Cat" goes on a Crépuscule tape
years.p: The Names played with Section 25 and A Certain Ratio. The same month, their self-produced "Cat" appeared on From Brussels With Love, the cassette that launched Les Disques du Crépuscule.

eras.title: Swimming with Hannett
eras.text: Brussels gave them a second home label in Crépuscule and Factory Benelux. They toured as a different band, became the first Belgians on John Peel's show, and went back to Stockport to make their only album of the era.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Sordinia moonlights in By Chance
years.p: A short-lived Brussels group on Crammed Discs, called "a sort of Belgian new wave supergroup". Its single "Soul Kitchen" had a B-side, "Revenge", that the Names later reworked.

years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: "Calcutta" on Factory Benelux, a year after "Nightshift"
years.p: FBN 9, cut in Brussels in May 1981 and remixed by Hannett in Manchester. NME found it "difficult to resist"; it sold fewer than FAC 29.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: As N.I.M., the Names play slow new songs to a Lyon crowd
years.p: On Crépuscule's Dialogue North-South package tour with [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]], [[Minny Pops|68142098-e3b3-4f76-a8cc-8898713fcf58]] and [[Paul Haig|ed5d5eef-b24b-4d5a-b899-f87dd8f4dd8c]], they played as Names in Mutation: "Music for Someone" and the slow "night" songs for the coming album. In Lyon, the crowd wanted the Factory singles.
years.xp: The tour ended at the Venue in London on February 16. NME's Chris Bohn wrote that they "swaddle tasteful, tame rhythms with suffocating synthesised cotton wool blankets."

years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: The first Belgians on John Peel's show
years.p: The day after the Venue, the Names recorded a BBC session for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]].

years.cap: The Names at Der Hallen, Leuven, February 8, 1982
q: We wished some things had been different.
years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: Swimming
years.h: Hannett splits Swimming into a day side and a night side
years.p: Made at Strawberry with Hannett, who wouldn't hear the songs beforehand, and led by piano. Crépuscule released it while Hannett was in dispute with Factory.
years.xp:
The band wanted "small sounds, big consequences". Sordinia had reservations: "The drums were recorded artificially, in pieces." The water sounds that link the tracks made it hard for radio to pull songs out.

The British press mostly passed. The Face praised "an intelligent, imaginative Martin Hannett production."

eras.title: The Astronaut, after the end
eras.text: A motorbike accident took out the drummer, and the members were finishing degrees with no money coming in. The last single came out after they'd stopped.

years.src: LTM: The Names · El Garaje de Frank
years.h: Luc Capelle's motorbike crash; Hannett comes to Brussels
years.p: With Michel Silverstein filling in on drums, the Names recorded "The Astronaut" in Brussels with Hannett.

years.src: LTM: The Names · El Garaje de Frank
years.h: "The Astronaut" comes out after the Names have split
years.p: A Crépuscule 12-inch, TWI 111, with "Revenge" and "Shining Hours". Some copies were pressed on green vinyl.
years.xp: "Music couldn't provide enough to live on. We had to find a honest job," the band told El Garaje de Frank. Sordinia became a film critic, wrote books on [[Terry Gilliam|7fc7a75a-fd8e-4c58-9072-7fa1873ceb3a]] and Nagisa Oshima and later directed. Deprez joined the civil service. Den Tandt went to Yale on a scholarship and went on to teach literature at the ULB in Brussels.

eras.title: Back as Jazz
eras.text: Factory Benelux put the Names back in print, and the original four tried again under a different name.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Swimming returns on CD with every single attached
years.p: Factory Benelux's reissue adds "Nightshift", "Calcutta", "The Astronaut", "Cat", "Music for Someone" and the Peel session.

years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: Calling themselves Jazz, the four make Nightvision
years.p: Nine new songs with bassist Eric De Bruyne, barely distributed outside Belgium. Sordinia on the name: "Another bad decision."

eras.title: Plan K again
eras.text: A Factory night at the club where it started brought the Names back for good. They've made records on and off since, with a new rhythm section around Sordinia and Deprez.

years.src: LTM: The Names · El Garaje de Frank
years.h: The Names reunite at Plan K for a Factory night
years.p: A Factory Night (Once Again) put them back on the Brussels stage with Section 25, Crispy Ambulance, Peter Hook and Kevin Hewick, to a packed room. The full set came out on the DVD Nightshift.

years.cap: The Names at Plan K, Brussels, December 12, 2009
years.src: LTM: The Names · Wikipedia: The Names
years.h: Monsters Next Door, and Den Tandt leaves
years.p: The first new Names album in 27 years came out on Str8line, with European dates. Den Tandt left at the end of the year.

years.src: LTM: The Names
years.h: Stranger Than You wears a 1982 painting
years.p: Factory Benelux, FBN 119, crowdfunded through PledgeMusic. The cover is a Benoît Hennebert painting first drawn up for Swimming; all 16 songs are Sordinia's.
years.xp: "There's a strong element of reconnection," Sordinia said, but also "developing your own legitimate strangeness." The band was now Sordinia, Deprez, drummer Laurent Loddewyckx and keyboardist Christophe Boulenger.

years.cap: The Names in an official band photo
years.src: Side-Line
years.h: Encore!, their first album in more than seven years
years.p: Out on Spleen+, preceded by the single "Far From the Factories".

sources.title: El Garaje de Frank: Interview, The Names
Side-Line: The Names announce new album Encore!
